title: Compatible finite-descent germs have constant stalk coordinates
statement: Let f: X prime → X be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], G a sheaf of sets [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] on the small etale site of X [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and x: Spec Ω → X a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. For each lift t of x along f let c_t be a bijection from the stalk of f inverse G at t to G_x [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], satisfying c_t(r_t(η_x(a))) = a for every a in G_x, where r_t is restriction of germs along base change [lem-weil-pbc-sets-finite-pushforward-stalk] and η is the inverse-image adjunction unit [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. If s prime is a section of f inverse G on X prime whose comparison pullbacks along the two projections of X prime ×_X X prime [def-pc-fibre-product] agree (transported along the pullback condition), then for every lift z of x to the identity etale object and every pair t,v of lifts along f, c_t(r_t([s prime]_z)) = c_v(r_v([s prime]_z)). No surjectivity of f is required.

proof.text: The germ-compatible inverse-image bijections identify each coordinate with the stalk of G. The composition-unit formula, transported through the fibre-product universal property, identifies the two comparison maps with the two projections on the set of pairs of geometric lifts. Applying compatibility and the bijectivity of the composite inverse-image germ map gives equality of the two chosen coordinates.

theorem finiteSurjectiveSetDescent_coordinates_constant
    {X X' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X' ⟶ X) [IsFinite f]
    (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)))
    (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X)
    (c : ∀ t : {t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X' // t ≫ f = x},
      (Scheme.pointSmallEtale t.1).sheafFiber.obj ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback f).obj G) →
        (Scheme.pointSmallEtale x).sheafFiber.obj G)
    (hc : ∀ t, Function.Bijective (c t))
    (hdiag : ∀ t a, c t ((colimit.pre
          ((CategoryOfElements.π (Scheme.pointSmallEtale t.1).fiber).op ⋙
            ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback f).obj G).obj)
          (Etale.baseChangeNbhd f x t).op) ((Scheme.pointSmallEtale x).sheafFiber.map
            ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
              (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ f) (Type (u + 1))
              (X.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
              (X'.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)).unit.app G) a)) = a)
    (s' : ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback f).obj G).obj.obj
      (op ((MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ f).obj
        (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)))))
    (hs :
        etaleSetDescentComparison f (pullback.fst f f) G (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) s' =
          eqToHom (congrArg
            (fun k : pullback f f ⟶ X ↦ ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback k).obj G).obj.obj
              (op ((MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ k).obj
                (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))))) (pullback.condition (f := f) (g := f)).symm)
            (etaleSetDescentComparison f (pullback.snd f f) G
              (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) s'))
    (z : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale x).fiber.obj (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))) :
    ∀ t v : {t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X' // t ≫ f = x},
      c t ((colimit.pre
          ((CategoryOfElements.π (Scheme.pointSmallEtale t.1).fiber).op ⋙
            ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback f).obj G).obj)
          (Etale.baseChangeNbhd f x t).op)
        ((Scheme.pointSmallEtale x).toPresheafFiber (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) z
      ((f.Etale.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        X.smallEtaleTopology X'.smallEtaleTopology).obj
          ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback f).obj G)).obj s')) =
      c v ((colimit.pre
          ((CategoryOfElements.π (Scheme.pointSmallEtale v.1).fiber).op ⋙
            ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback f).obj G).obj)
          (Etale.baseChangeNbhd f x v).op)
        ((Scheme.pointSmallEtale x).toPresheafFiber (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) z
      ((f.Etale.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        X.smallEtaleTopology X'.smallEtaleTopology).obj
          ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback f).obj G)).obj s'))
